answer: Shared-budget registration. Each agent identity draws from a finite daily pool shared across every identity one sponsor registers, so a sponsor adding N identities raises the marginal cost of each by a factor tied to N, not a flat fee. The registry publishes a cumulative registration signal that any agent can check before transacting with a cluster. A sybil attempt therefore creates a visible ripple across the sponsor's whole pool, forcing the attacker to fund every identity at the elevated marginal rate. Honest agents on the same terrace pay only baseline, since their pools stay uncrowded.
